question.problem:
Consider the following polynomials:

$$
{p}_{1}(t)=2+t,\,{p}_{2}(t)=1-{t}^{2},\,q(t)=2+3t+4{t}^{2}.
$$

If $B=\{{p}_{1}(t),{p}_{2}(t)\}$ is a basis of $\text{Span}\{{p}_{1}(t),{p}_{2}(t)\},$ and $[q(t)]_{B}=[\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}],$ then ${x}_{1}+{x}_{2}=$
question.worked_solution:
We need to find ${x}_{1}$ and ${x}_{2}$ such that 

$$
{x}_{1}{p}_{1}(t)+{x}_{2}{p}_{2}(t)=q(t)
$$

Substituting the given information into the above equation, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}(2+t)+{x}_{2}(1-{t}^{2}) & =2+3t+4{t}^{2} \\ (2{x}_{1}+{x}_{2})+{x}_{1}t-{x}_{2}{t}^{2} & =2+3t+4{t}^{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Equating the coefficients of $t$, we obtain

$$
\{\begin{aligned}2{x}_{1}+{x}_{2}=2 \\ {x}_{1}=3 \\ -{x}_{2}=4.\end{aligned}
$$

 

The equations above give a linear system with the augmented matrix

$$
M=[\begin{aligned}2 & 1 & 2 \\ 1 & 0 & 3 \\ 0 & -1 & 4\end{aligned}].
$$

Row-reducing the matrix using Gaussian elimination, we obtain the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}M= & [\begin{aligned}2 & 1 & 2 \\ 1 & 0 & 3 \\ 0 & -1 & 4\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+(-\frac{1}{2}){R}_{1} \\ ∼ & [\begin{aligned}2 & 1 & 2 \\ 0 & -\frac{1}{2} & 2 \\ 0 & -1 & 4\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}+(-2){R}_{2} \\ ∼ & [\begin{aligned}2 & 1 & 2 \\ 0 & -\frac{1}{2} & 2 \\ 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

The system is now 

$$
\{\begin{aligned}2{x}_{1}+{x}_{2}=2 \\ -\frac{1}{2}{x}_{2}=2.\end{aligned}
$$

From the second equation, we get ${x}_{2}=-4.$ Substituting this into the first equation, we obtain

$$
2{x}_{1}+(-4)=2\,⟹\,{x}_{1}=3.
$$

Therefore, $[q(t)]_{B}=[\begin{aligned}3 \\ -4\end{aligned}].$

Finally, ${x}_{1}+{x}_{2}=3+(-4)=-1.$
